reading.body:
OptimumHQ is a software company mistagged as a data center, and Arizona's 56 mapped data center facilities include only 4 that publish power figures, totaling 512 MW.

The company builds AI-powered ERP, CRM, and business-automation tools for small and midsize businesses. No power draw, operator, or server specifications are recorded for it. Its own site lists an office in Gilbert, while the address on file is in Mesa, on the same road that runs through both cities. Research points to a shared multi-tenant building rather than dedicated infrastructure, and nothing indicates servers at either address.

For AI scaling, the more useful half of that first sentence is the Arizona count. Power consumption is the number that ties a building to the grid, and almost none of the state's tagged facilities disclose it. The 512 MW covers four facilities, not the state. Treating all 56 rows as comparable would put software offices in the same column as real facilities.

This does not establish Arizona's actual data center capacity or its load on the grid. It does not show that the other 52 facilities lack power infrastructure, only that they do not publish figures. And it cannot say how many other rows are mistagged the same way, because a single corrected entry is not a measure of the error rate.
